newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open lower, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open lower, seen consolidating.

text.p: Singapore shares opened slightly lower on Monday as last week's profit-taking and trading corrections continued.
Dealers said they expected consolidation to be the primary feature of the early part of the week.
"This week fund-managers are likely to look at the market for a second time and see where profits can be taken," said a dealer with a local firm.
"The blue chip laggards will be picked up," he predicted.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials index stood at 2186.91 at 0220 GMT, down 6.73 points from Friday's close.
Early activity saw traded volume at 33.92 million shares with 93 gainers against 89 losers.
One dealer attributed much early activity to married deals, the biggest of which was a 5.01 million off-market cross in Hotel Properties at Singapore $2.35.
F.J. Benjamin, last week's new listing, was active with 1.85 million shares traded as the stock lost two cents to S$1.11.
Malaysian share trading was expected to be heavy this week, reflecting a switch from the activity in Singapore shares last week, another dealer said.
